correctness.rationale: For any two strictly positive independent Schaefer stocks with positive net growth, the exact logistic solutions reduce the normalized CPUE-minus-biomass sign to the difference of two individual normalized logistic factors. Clearing their strictly positive denominators gives a constant plus two exponentials, zero at \(t=0\), whose derivative has at most one positive zero; Rolle yields at most one further positive zero and forces any such zero to be simple. The three-stock integer witness has valid growth rates (17,1,3), exact cleared polynomial the degree-20 integer polynomial given in RESULT.md, and all denominators positive on (0,1). After removing \(z-1\) and \(z/(1-z)\) substitution, 20 exact coefficients give two sign variations, so at most two roots; exact signs at \(z=9/10,1/3,1/100\) force two. Standalone standard-library checker.py independently passes 40 exact arithmetic assertions for the coefficient identity, Descartes transform, sample ODE and signs. No finite experiment substitutes for the global proof.

originality.rationale: The full inspected Kleiber–Maunder primary study proves initial hyperresponsiveness and derives eventual equilibrium conditions, with one-crossing two-stock illustrations and two-stock regressions. Those implications do not prove the at-most-one theorem for every strictly positive initial state or imply the exactly-two-crossing three-stock certificate. Searches of published mathematical results surfaced different harvest, population and indicator questions but no same CPUE/biomass temporal crossing claim. The most plausible 1991 antecedent could not be compared in full, and mathematical exponential-sum literature may contain equivalent formulations; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The source-level mathematical gap concerns repeated time reversals of an important aggregate CPUE proxy, not a re-labeled logistic trajectory. Sharp two-vs-three stock complexity demonstrates that even perfectly proportional species catch rates can combine into an indicator whose relative bias changes direction twice after a fixed-effort perturbation. It gives an exact structural limitation for two-stock surrogate assessments and a reproducible three-stock counterexample. Practical prevalence, noise sensitivity, and spatial effects are explicitly not claimed.
